nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Defines the repository-wide engineering contract for BeneBot, including its synthetic-only scope, historical-versus-current evidence boundary, server-side integrations, deterministic billing math, security rules, and validation gates.

nodes.name: BENEBOT_BUILD_SPEC.md
nodes.summary: Canonical end-to-end specification for BeneBot's Jane Doe demo, covering architecture, FHIR resources, deterministic bill normalization, signed sessions, Deepgram voice, Stedi eligibility, resource search, Medplum writes, UI contracts, testing, and phased delivery.
nodes.languageNotes: The Markdown specification combines normative requirements, TypeScript and JSON contract examples, route definitions, trust boundaries, and a complete implementation sequence.

nodes.name: BENEBOT_RESEARCH_AGENT_PROMPTS.md
nodes.summary: Defines six bounded research lanes and a final independent adjudication prompt for producing BeneBot's authoritative bilingual concept, misconception, utterance, rubric, and tool-prerequisite packet.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Redirects Claude-compatible agents to the canonical repository instructions in AGENTS.md so all coding assistants share the same safety and delivery constraints.

nodes.name: CODEX_START_PROMPT.md
nodes.summary: Provides a copy-ready kickoff prompt that tells Codex to ground itself in the build specification, execute one phase at a time, preserve strict evidence boundaries, and run each required validation gate.

nodes.name: CONVERSATION_RELIABILITY_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Plans the bounded reliability layer for BeneBot conversations: eight phase-aware rubrics, closed-tool prerequisites, deterministic enforcement, an adjudicated bilingual concept library, evidence-linked transcript evaluation, and staged integration.

nodes.name: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Translates the build specification into a time-boxed Spanish-first hackathon execution plan with fixed technical choices, staged work waves, validation checkpoints, demo choreography, and an explicit fallback-and-cut ladder.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operational runbook for installing, configuring, seeding, testing, and rehearsing BeneBot, with explicit setup instructions for Medplum, Deepgram, and Stedi plus honest degraded-mode behavior and the Spanish-first demo script.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Defines the private Next.js application package, its development, type-check, Vitest, Playwright, build, and Medplum seed scripts, and runtime dependencies for Deepgram UI, Medplum FHIR, JWT handling, and Zod validation.

nodes.name: spanish-concept-library.json
nodes.summary: Stores six es-419 medical-billing concepts with preferred and alternative terminology, patient-facing explanations, confusion repairs, bounded analogies, comprehension checks, utterance variants, forbidden claims, and pronunciation guidance.
nodes.languageNotes: The JSON models neutral Latin American Spanish as structured runtime guidance rather than direct English translation, with explicit false-claim and TTS safeguards.

nodes.name: spanish-review-notes.md
nodes.summary: Records the linguistic review rationale behind the Spanish concept library, including U.S. Latino regional choices, billing-term distinctions, false friends, remaining ambiguities, and pronunciation guidance for voice output.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Configures strict TypeScript checking for the Next.js application with ESNext modules, React JSX, incremental compilation, the @ path alias, and generated Next.js type inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Strict mode and noEmit make TypeScript a validation gate while Next.js retains control of bundling and emitted artifacts.
